title: What if all the salt left the sea tonight?

layers.text: What if all the
salt
left the sea tonight?
You're fishing in Bergen harbor, Norway.

scenes.notes: Frame 1 = cover: bright moonlit Bryggen, moon reflection with ripples, orange current ribbon (plant), you with a rod. Title clears 6.6-7.0. [screen 0.0-8.0 s]
9-frame white flash (8.0-8.3); salt glints burst off the water and wink out; HUD salt 35.0 -> 0.0 in 1 s; chapter THE WATER. [screen 8.0-9.0 s]

layers.text: The spray on your lips tastes like rain.

scenes.notes: Body first: spray on your lips tastes like rain. Glyphs only, no text. [screen 9.0-14.0 s]

layers.markup: <svg viewBox="0 0 120 110" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M10 10 H100 L92 100 H18 Z" fill="#c9d3dc" stroke="#5b6b73" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M100 30 Q125 45 98 70" fill="none" stroke="#5b6b73" stroke-width="7"/><rect x="16" y="30" width="80" height="62" fill="#bfeaff" opacity=".8"/></svg>

layers.text: The whole sea is drinkable now.

scenes.notes: False resolution: a tin cup dips into the harbour and comes up clear; HUD 2.2 BILLION LACK SAFE WATER at 14.5. [screen 14.0-19.5 s]

layers.text: But fish blood is saltier than this water.
So the fish swell.

scenes.notes: Rule caption 4 at 19.5 (chapter THE FISH at 20.0); caption 5 at 24.0; fish start to swell at 24.0. [screen 19.5-27.0 s]
Textless: the school breaks apart and sinks past the kelp. [screen 27.0-31.0 s]

layers.text: Nearly every sea animal dies before dawn.

scenes.notes: Nearly every sea animal dies before dawn: whole-column cross-section, everything settling. Chapter THE PEOPLE at 33.0. [screen 31.0-34.5 s]

layers.text: You're now saltier than the ocean.

scenes.notes: Return-to-you dip at 43%: two icon bars, you (tall) vs the sea (empty). No text. [screen 34.5-38.0 s]

layers.text: 3.2 billion people rely on fish protein.

scenes.notes: 3.2 billion: 32 figures (1 = 100 million) with fish glyphs that grey out from 40.0. [screen 38.0-41.0 s]
White salt crystals fill the frame, then pure white. No new text; HUD drawn in ink colour. [screen 41.0-43.0 s]

layers.text: Sinking salty water up north helps pull it.

scenes.notes: Scale jump: Bergen pin -> North Atlantic; Gulf Stream path draws Florida Straits -> Bergen (plant named). Chapter THE CURRENT; meter SALT GONE. [screen 43.0-47.0 s]

layers.text: Sinking salty water up north helps pull it.
Icy fresh water floats.

scenes.notes: Captions 9 (45.0, in previous shot) and 10 (51.0). Sinking rings pulse, then stop and grey at 51.0. HEAT CARRIED NORTH held. [screen 47.0-55.0 s]
NORTHERN SINKING: STOPPED. Rings fade; the path keeps flowing but thins north of 55N only (wind-driven part continues). [screen 55.0-59.0 s]
Dive back into the Bergen pin as a dawn glow sweeps from the east; master clock runs out. [screen 59.0-62.0 s]

layers.text: Sunrise. The sea looks normal.

scenes.notes: Bookend of shot 1 at dawn: the sea looks normal, boats head out, you reel in an empty hook (bathos, no text). BOATS OUT / BERGEN, 6 HOURS LATER. [screen 62.0-66.0 s]

layers.text: But that current kept your winters mild.

scenes.notes: Twist on the viewer: same quay in snow, FIRST WINTER; current ribbon thin and pale. One HUD line at 67.0. [screen 66.0-71.0 s]

layers.text: What if all the
salt
left the sea tonight?

12,900 YEARS AGO, MELTWATER LIKELY STALLED THIS CURRENT.
EUROPE TURNED ICE-AGE COLD FOR 1,200 YEARS.

scenes.notes: Exact title repeat + Younger Dryas fact (not read). [screen 73.0-80.0 s]
